issues.claim: price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve = "$0-$250/month with a $0-$449 entry setup fee"
issues.problem: The band's stated ceiling is contradicted by prices cited inside the same field: Insurance Agent App Plan F at $399/month and Plan G at $549/month (both confirmed in the insuranceagencytools.com table), plus Deskpilot AI Agency Partner at $2,500+/mo is mentioned elsewhere in the brief. As written, the $250 ceiling does not follow from the prices listed under it. The inference_note narrows the ceiling to entry plans, but the range string itself is not scoped that way and reads as a market ceiling.
issues.fix: Rescope the band: "Entry plans $0-$250/month with a $0-$449 entry setup fee (larger tiers of the same products run to $549/month on Insurance Agent App and $2,500+/mo on Deskpilot)", or raise the band ceiling to $549 and state that it is an entry-plan band.

issues.claim: price_ranges.mid_market = "$450-$1,000/month for a per-seat AI operations platform ... that issues certificates and can write back to the AMS"
issues.problem: The band membership ($497/$997/$497) is correct, but the qualifying description is not supported by the sourced pages. COIflow Network, confirmed on coiflow.app, lists "API & AMS export" (export only, not write-back), and PolisAgent lists "AMS integration architecture" and "custom integrations" only on Enterprise at $1,997/month, with lower tiers ingesting a CSV export from the AMS (confirmed on polisagent.com). "Per-seat" also does not describe COIflow, which is priced by certificate allowance. The inference's reasoning therefore contradicts the brief's own sourced facts.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "$450-$1,000/month for an AI operations platform that issues certificates within an agency workflow — PolisAgent $497/$997 (CSV ingest; AMS write-back only at the $1,997 Enterprise tier) and COIflow Network $497 (API/AMS export)". Drop "per-seat" or limit it to PolisAgent.

issues.claim: Certificial entry: "A vendor case study (Synatic) describes a separate integration project to connect an agency's AMS to the Certificial network, and notes live coverage monitoring only applies to suppliers whose agencies are already connected."
issues.problem: The Synatic/McMichael case study, re-read in full, does not say that monitoring is limited to connected agencies. That statement appears in coisoftware.com/blog/certificial-pricing ("you only get live monitoring on the connected ones"), which the brief cites elsewhere. The sentence misattributes a third-party analyst's point to the vendor case study.
issues.fix: Split the sentence: keep the Synatic case study for the AMS-to-Certificial integration project and for the endorsement/AMS-data lag, and attribute the connected-agency monitoring limitation to coisoftware.com/blog/certificial-pricing.

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs item 2 (Clermont: $33.33/hour CSR, $5.56 per standard certificate, ~$3,600/month at 650 certificates) and item 3 ($3-$7 per transaction, $1,200-$2,000 part-time and $2,500-$4,000 full-time desks), year "2026"
issues.problem: The numbers are all confirmed on clermontglobal.com/blog/coi-processing-cost-comparison.html, but they are a vendor's own worked model and its estimate of competitors' rates, not buyer-reported costs, and the blog carries no publication date, so "2026" is the access year rather than the source's date. Filing them under buyer_reported_costs risks the orchestrator treating a vendor model as independent buyer evidence.
issues.fix: Move both items to a separate "vendor_cost_models" section, or retitle the year field as "undated vendor blog, accessed 2026" and add "vendor model, not buyer invoice" to each finding line rather than only to context.

issues.claim: Certificial Requestor Basic tier: "$0/mo — up to 5 suppliers" with includes "Track compliance of up to 5 suppliers; 'Try it Free'"
issues.problem: The vendor page as fetched on 2026-11-12 renders only the free-tier sentence ("free for Insureds, Agents and Brokers, and Requestors with up to 5 Insureds") and does not render the plan cards, so "5 suppliers", the plan name "Requestor Basic" and "Try it Free" come from the third-party compilations, not a direct read. The price field flags this for the supplier count but the includes field states it unlabelled, and the $0 carries a "/mo" unit the vendor page does not state.
issues.fix: Mark the includes line "(per third-party compilation; vendor page states only 'up to 5 Insureds')" and drop the "/mo" unit from the Requestor Basic price, matching how the Agent/Broker tier already handles the unstated billing term.

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs items 4-7: Reddit-reported Applied Epic $230-$270/user/month, $200+ per added user plus $800 setup, $40/month COI tracking tool
issues.problem: The Reddit threads themselves could not be opened by me either (reddit.com returns no readable content), so the figures cannot be confirmed against the primary thread. A search-result summary reproduced the $230/user/month figure with the 500+ user context and the $240 / $270-additional-user figures, but the $1,300 first-user quote and the $800 new-user setup fee did not surface in my searches. The brief already discloses this limitation in both the context fields and the caveats.
issues.fix: No change needed for the disclosed limitation, but the $1,300 first-user figure and the $800 setup fee should carry an explicit "not reproduced in a second search" note, or be dropped, since only the $230/$240/$270 figures were independently resurfaced.
